title: ALMA Observations of Supernova Remnant N49 in the Large Magellanic Cloud. II. Non-LTE Analysis of Shock-heated Molecular Clouds
question: What are the H$_2$ number density and kinetic temperature of molecular clouds in the vicinity of the LMC supernova remnant N49, and are they heated by supernova shocks or cosmic rays?

data.arrays: 12 m array, 7 m array, Total Power (TP) array

what.value: Primary-beam-corrected ALMA 12CO(J=1-0) cleaned data and cloud definitions/positions

evidence.quote: An important breakthrough came from observations of the $^{12}$CO($J$ = 1–0) emission line by (cite: 2018ApJ...863...55Y) using the Atacama Large Millimeter/Submillimeter Array (ALMA).
In order to take an intensity ratio of two different CO $J$-transitions, we also used the primary-beam-corrected, $^{12}$CO($J$ = 1–0) cleaned data published in .
Col. (1): Cloud name defined by . Cols. (2, 3): Position of the maximum intensity of $^{12}$CO($J$ = 1–0) .

what.value: Low metal elemental abundances for the LMC used in the PDR model

evidence.loc: APPENDIX Time evolution of the kinetic temperature
evidence.quote: Elemental abundances are taken from (cite: 2015ApJ...812..142A) (low metal abundances for the LMC in their Table 1).

what.value: UV intensity G0 = 110 used in the PDR model

evidence.loc: APPENDIX Time evolution of the kinetic temperature
evidence.quote: As input parameters for the model, we employ the UV intensity $G_0$ = $110$ (cite: 2012ApJ...744..160S) and the hydrogen (Hi+H$_2$) gas density $n_{\mathrm{HI+H_2}}$ = $1\times10^3$ cm$^{-3}$.

recipe.goal: Image and combine multi-array ALMA CO data and smooth to a common resolution
recipe.method: Apply multiscale CLEAN with natural weighting in tclean, combine 7m+TP for CO(3-2) and 12m+7m for CO(2-1) using feather, apply primary beam correction, and smooth all CO cubes to a 3.5'' x 3.5'' beam
key_parameters: Velocity resolution 0.4 km s^-1; PB threshold 0.2 for 12CO(2-1) and 0.5 for 12CO(3-2) and 13CO(2-1); smoothed beam 3.5'' x 3.5''

recipe.goal: Measure cloud line parameters, sizes, virial masses, and CO intensity ratios
recipe.method: Identify eight clouds detected in 13CO(2-1) at >= 3 sigma, fit single Gaussian profiles to CO spectra, measure cloud sizes from the half-peak integrated intensity contour area, compute virial masses, and map the 12CO(2-1)/12CO(1-0) ratio
key_parameters: Velocity range V_LSR = 285.5-287.8 km s^-1 for peak intensity maps
assumptions: Virial equilibrium for cloud mass estimation

recipe.goal: Derive kinetic temperature and H2 number density via non-LTE LVG analysis
recipe.method: Perform non-LTE radiative transfer calculations using the Large Velocity Gradient (LVG) approximation on 12CO(2-1), 12CO(3-2), and 13CO(2-1) line intensities for each of the eight clouds
key_parameters: Individual velocity gradient dv/dr calculated for each cloud from HMHW linewidth dv and cloud radius dr
assumptions: Isothermal spherical cloud with uniform photon escape probability and velocity gradient dv/dr

recipe.goal: Fit X-ray shell geometry and T_kin vs n(H2) correlation
recipe.method: Reprocess archival Chandra data to create a 0.5-7.0 keV flux image, fit radial X-ray profile with a 3D spherical Gaussian shell model, and fit the T_kin vs n(H2) relation for clouds N, O, P, Q, R using MPFITEXY
key_parameters: SNR geometric center at (05h25m59.57s, -66d04m56.4s); X-ray energy band 0.5-7.0 keV
assumptions: Three-dimensional spherical shell geometry with Gaussian radial profile

recipe.goal: Model cosmic-ray diffusion and time evolution of gas temperature in a PDR
recipe.method: Calculate cosmic-ray diffusion length and run 1D plane-parallel PDR models over two stages (10^7 yr pre-SN at standard cosmic-ray ionization rate, then 10^5 yr post-SN with enhanced ionization rates) to track T_kin at the cloud center (A_V = 5 mag)
key_parameters: t_age = 1.5 x 10^11 s, E = 100 MeV, B = 10 uG for diffusion; G_0 = 110, n_(HI+H2) = 1 x 10^3 cm^-3, N_H/A_V = 3.5 x 10^21 cm^-2, A_V = 5 mag, zeta = 3 x 10^-17 to 1 x 10^-14 s^-1 for PDR model
assumptions: LMC low metal abundances; initially all H in H2, all C in CO, remaining O in H2O ice

evidence.quote: We find a high intensity ratio of $R_\mathrm{2-1/1-0}$ $\sim$1.0–1.2 in the entire molecular cloud associated with the SNR.

evidence.quote: We obtained a shell radius of $7.7 \pm 1.8$ pc and shell thickness of $2.6 \pm 4.5$ pc as the best-fit parameters of the fitting, where the shell thickness was defined as the FWHM of the Gaussian function.

We obtained a shell radius of $7.7 \pm 1.8$ pc and shell thickness of $2.6 \pm 4.5$ pc as the best-fit parameters of the fitting, where the shell thickness was defined as the FWHM of the Gaussian function.

Adopting $t_\mathrm{age} = 1.5 \times 10^{11}$ s (cite: 2012ApJ...748..117P), $E = 100$ MeV, and $B = 10~\mu$G, we obtain $l_\mathrm{diff} \sim$6 pc which is substantially larger than the maximum separation between cloud P and the shock boundary of the SNR.

score_reason: ALMA project codes, Chandra ObsIDs, calibrators, beam sizes, RMS sensitivities, smoothing resolution (3.5''), cloud coordinates, Gaussian line parameters, and LVG assumptions ([12CO/H2], [12CO/13CO], dv/dr definition) are clearly tabulated and described, though the specific LVG code and detailed tclean parameters are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: Public archival ALMA data (#2015.1.01195.S and #2021.2.00008.S) and explicit cloud coordinates/apertures in Table 1 allow direct independent extraction of CO spectra, Gaussian line fits, and non-LTE LVG derivation of T_kin and n(H2) for the eight clouds.
